conventions.convention: Finite integers d,T≥1; 0<β_t<1; α_t=1−β_t; barα_0=1 and barα_t is the product of α_s for s=1,…,t. Reverse means are finite-valued Borel maps and reverse variances are fixed positive finite numbers.

The conditioned Gaussian posterior formula applies only for t≥2. At t=1, conditioning on x_0 produces a point mass; the learned reconstruction likelihood remains a separate positive-variance Gaussian density. Conditioning additionally on x_0 does not establish Gaussianity of the unconditional reverse law.
KL is directional: D_KL(Q‖P) integrates the log density ratio under Q. Gaussian covariance arguments v and w are variances, and log is the natural logarithm. AC is assumed.

The exact ELBO identity requires a finite positive marginal likelihood, forward-to-posterior absolute continuity, and absolute integrability of both log path densities. The finite-horizon terminal-prior KL is retained. The simple loss averages unweighted noise errors over all t=1,…,T.

Data and time indices are independently uniform on their nonempty finite index sets; Gaussian noise is independent of both. Weighted branches multiply the selected decoder or interior contribution by T and add the terminal KL once. Each mode has its own integrability requirements.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and the finite Gaussian forward chain. For each fixed x_0 and 1≤t≤T, q(x_t|x_0)=N_d(√barα_t x_0,(1−barα_t)I_d). For 2≤t≤T, q(x_{t−1}|x_t,x_0) is Gaussian with mean [√barα_{t−1} β_t x_0+√α_t(1−barα_{t−1})x_t]/(1−barα_t) and covariance [β_t(1−barα_{t−1})/(1−barα_t)]I_d.

Under AC and the stated finite-chain, Borel-mean, positive-variance, support and log-integrability hypotheses, log p_θ(x_0)=ELBO_θ(x_0)+D_KL(Q_{x_0}‖Π_{θ,x_0}), with nonnegative KL. The negative ELBO equals terminal-prior KL plus expected negative reconstruction log likelihood plus the sum of expected conditioned-posterior-to-reverse-kernel KL terms for t=2,…,T. In the epsilon parameterization each interior term is E[w_t‖ε−ε_θ(x_t,t)‖²+C_t], where w_t=β_t²/[2σ_t²α_t(1−barα_t)] and C_t=d[tildeβ_t/σ_t²−1+log(σ_t²/tildeβ_t)]/2. The unweighted simple loss is not in general the exact maximum-likelihood objective.

Assume AC. The forward path density for fixed x_0 is the product, over t=1,…,T, of Gaussian transition densities with mean √α_t x_{t−1} and covariance β_t I_d. The reverse joint density is a standard Gaussian prior at x_T times Gaussian reverse transition densities with finite-valued Borel means and fixed positive finite variances.
Assume AC. Let d≥1, m,n∈R^d, and v,w>0. If Q=N_d(m,vI_d) and P=N_d(n,wI_d), then D_KL(Q‖P)=d(v/w−1+log(w/v))/2+‖m−n‖²/(2w).

Assume AC and admissible estimator inputs. The returned real random variable Y has finite expectation. In simple mode E[Y]=N⁻¹Σ_i L_simple(θ;x_0^(i)); in weighted-elbo mode E[Y]=N⁻¹Σ_i[−ELBO_θ(x_0^(i))]. Both identities include N=1 and T=1.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit inherited choice assumption in Gaussian, KL and ELBO interfaces.
The reference measures underlying the Gaussian path densities.
Gaussian projection characterization, specified means and covariances, and finite second moments.
Identification of finite product Lebesgue integration with Euclidean path-space integration on Borel sets; AC supplies its countable-choice assumption.
Existence and rectangle identities for finite product reference measures.
Successive integration and normalization of nonnegative Gaussian transition products.
Strictly positive Gaussian density formulas for positive-definite covariances.
Expectation conventions and finite integrability of objective estimators.
Directional Radon–Nikodym log-ratio convention and its AC hypothesis.
Natural-logarithm convention in Gaussian densities and divergences.
Joint Gaussianity of finite innovation stacks and adjacent-state constructions, including singular covariance blocks.
Conditional mean and Schur-complement covariance with positive-definite observed covariance.
Pushforward probability-law convention in the path-space ELBO application.
Finite positive normalizer, support condition, absolute log-integrability and finite ELBO definition.
Exact evidence/ELBO/reverse-KL identity and nonnegativity under AC.
